title: season
description: The season at block and month scale (#139). A BLOCK is a maximal run of consecutive training weeks closed by an absence of `gap_weeks` or more calendar weeks carrying no load — see ADR 0011. That boundary is used because it is the only one in the data that is not a judgment call: textbook build/recover cycle detection fits 8-10 of 96 real training weeks depending on how adjacency is read, so a detector built on it segments noise. Blocks are DESCRIBED and never named — there is no `base`/`build`/`peak` field, because those are claims about intent and load observes only volume (#154). `slope_tss_per_week` is the regression slope of weekly load across the block, and `fitted_start_load`/`fitted_end_load` are where that line begins and ends — READ THOSE FIRST. `trend_r2` is how much of the week-to-week SCATTER the line explains, and a low value does NOT mean the block had no trend: it means the weeks varied a lot around the line. On real data a block at r2 0.10 still fell from 315 to 214 TSS/week across 71 weeks. Judge the slope against `weeks`, not against r2 alone. A block whose trailing week is still in progress excludes that partial week from the regression (its load is a partial sum, and leaving it in swung the slope by half on a single session) while still counting it in `weeks`, `sessions` and `total_load`. Both are withheld (`trend_known: false`) under three weeks, where r2 is 1 by construction. A long block is reported as long and never subdivided — splitting it would fabricate the boundary this definition exists to avoid. `weeks` counts weeks WITH training while `span_weeks` counts the calendar weeks the block covers; they differ wherever a rest week sits inside a block, and `mean_weekly_load` divides by `span_weeks` so it matches the dates. `closed: false` means no absence has ended the block — records simply stop — so its numbers are still moving and a single new session can change them substantially. `end_date` is the last day WITH training, never the end of its calendar week. `sessions` counts activities inside the block's window. It does NOT always equal the `months[]` total: an activity that produced no load and fell inside an absence belongs to a month and to no block, which is correct — blocks are training, months are the calendar. Polarization uses the same power-else-pace-else-HR-zone fallback `summary` and `zones` use, so it agrees with them over the same window. (`compare` computes its `easy_pct` from raw HR zones instead and can differ by several points on identical sessions — that is a pre-existing inconsistency in `compare`, not here.) `ftp_*` names the sport family it belongs to, because a rowing threshold and a cycling FTP are different quantities and an athlete may have both. `ftp_start`/`ftp_end` are CHRONOLOGICAL and are what to read: `ftp_lo`/`ftp_hi` are an unordered min/max and reading them left to right implies a direction they do not carry. `ftp_family_pct` is the winning family's share of sessions — near 50 it is a coin flip standing in for a mixed block, and the other family's threshold is not published. `months[].partial` marks a month still in progress, whose load must not be compared to a complete one.
